3. Wire markers into ring buffer

In hypergossip_model.rs, when you enqueue an event into the ring buffer:

impl SovereignGossip for HyperGossipModel {\n    fn push_event(&mut self, track_id: u8, midi_event: MidiEvent) {\n        let tick = self.clock.current_tick();\n        let echo_cycle = self.echo_cycle;\n        let marker = TemporalMarker {\n            id: uuid::Uuid::new_v4(),\n            track_id,\n            tick,\n            created_at: chrono::Utc::now(),\n            echo_cycle,\n        };\n\n        self.buffer.push((track_id, midi_event, marker));\n        self.emit_temporal_marker(marker);\n    }\n\n    fn emit_temporal_marker(&mut self, marker: TemporalMarker) {\n        self.time_machine_tx.send(marker).ok();\n    }\n}\n

4. Time Machine pallet ingestion

In pallet-time-machine/src/lib.rs:

  • Storage:

    • TemporalMarkers: map hasher(blake2_128) Uuid => TemporalMarker

    • TemporalDrift: map (TrackId, EchoCycle) => DriftStats

  • Call/Hook:

    • Expose fn ingest_temporal_marker(origin, marker: TemporalMarker) as an internal API (not an extrinsic) called from the runtime via a bridge module.

rust
pub struct DriftStats {\n    pub last_tick: u64,\n    pub drift_delta: i64,\n    pub stability: TemporalStability,\n}\n\nimpl<T: Config> Pallet<T> {\n    pub fn ingest_temporal_marker(marker: TemporalMarker) {\n        let key = (marker.track_id, marker.echo_cycle);\n        let mut stats = <TemporalDrift<T>>::get(key).unwrap_or(DriftStats {\n            last_tick: marker.tick,\n            drift_delta: 0,\n            stability: TemporalStability::Stable,\n        });\n\n        let delta = marker.tick as i64 - stats.last_tick as i64;\n        stats.drift_delta = delta;\n        stats.stability = classify_stability(delta);\n        stats.last_tick = marker.tick;\n\n        <TemporalDrift<T>>::insert(key, stats);\n        <TemporalMarkers<T>>::insert(marker.id, marker);\n    }\n}\n\nfn classify_stability(delta: i64) -> TemporalStability {\n    match delta.abs() {\n        0..=5 => TemporalStability::Stable,\n        6..=50 => TemporalStability::Metastable,\n        _ => TemporalStability::Chaotic,\n    }\n}\n

5. Integrate with verify_quorum

In council.rs, extend quorum checks:

rust
pub fn verify_quorum(request: &RollbackRequest) -> Result<(), QuorumError> {\n    // existing seat checks...\n\n    let drift_ok = TimeMachine::check_temporal_drift(request.target_block)?;\n    if !drift_ok {\n        return Err(QuorumError::TemporalDriftExceeded);\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n

Where check_temporal_drift inspects TemporalDrift for the relevant tracks and ensures no Chaotic stability in the rollback window.

Canonical TemporalMarker Protobuf & Cross‑Runtime Bindings

You said it—proceed with protobuf. Let’s lock this in as the canonical wire format.

1. temporal_marker.proto

Single source of truth for Rust, Go, Cloudflare, SpaceBook.

proto
syntax = \"proto3\";\n\npackage sovereign.temporal;\n\nenum TemporalStability {\n  STABILITY_UNSPECIFIED = 0;\n  STABLE                = 1;\n  CHAOTIC               = 2;\n  METASTABLE            = 3;\n}\n\nmessage TemporalMarker {\n  string id           = 1;  // UUID v4\n  uint32 track_id     = 2;  // 0–255\n  uint64 tick         = 3;  // logical or wall-clock tick\n  int64  created_at   = 4;  // Unix millis\n  uint32 echo_cycle   = 5;  // 7s cadence index\n  TemporalStability stability = 6;\n}\n

2. Rust Binding

Generate:

bash
protoc --rust_out=src/proto temporal_marker.proto\n

Usage in hypergossip_model.rs:

rust
use crate::proto::sovereign::temporal::TemporalMarker as PbTemporalMarker;\n\nfn to_pb_marker(m: &TemporalMarker, stability: TemporalStability) -> PbTemporalMarker {\n    PbTemporalMarker {\n        id: m.id.to_string(),\n        track_id: m.track_id as u32,\n        tick: m.tick,\n        created_at: m.created_at.timestamp_millis(),\n        echo_cycle: m.echo_cycle,\n        stability: match stability {\n            TemporalStability::Stable => TemporalStabilityPb::STABLE.into(),\n            TemporalStability::Chaotic => TemporalStabilityPb::CHAOTIC.into(),\n            TemporalStability::Metastable => TemporalStabilityPb::METASTABLE.into(),\n        },\n    }\n}\n

You can then send PbTemporalMarker over any transport (Substrate, TCP, QUIC, etc.).

3. Go Binding

Generate:

bash
protoc --go_out=./internal/proto temporal_marker.proto\n

Usage:

go
import sovereignpb \"your/module/internal/proto/sovereign/temporal\"\n\nfunc ToPbMarker(m TemporalMarker) *sovereignpb.TemporalMarker {\n    return &sovereignpb.TemporalMarker{\n        Id:         m.ID,\n        TrackId:    uint32(m.TrackID),\n        Tick:       m.Tick,\n        CreatedAt:  m.CreatedAt.UnixMilli(),\n        EchoCycle:  m.EchoCycle,\n        Stability:  toPbStability(m.Stability),\n    }\n}\n\nfunc toPbStability(s TemporalStability) sovereignpb.TemporalStability {\n    switch s {\n    case Stable:\n        return sovereignpb.TemporalStability_STABLE\n    case Chaotic:\n        return sovereignpb.TemporalStability_CHAOTIC\n    case Metastable:\n        return sovereignpb.TemporalStability_METASTABLE\n    default:\n        return sovereignpb.TemporalStability_STABILITY_UNSPECIFIED\n    }\n}\n

4. Cloudflare / JS Binding

Use protobufjs (or similar):

js
import { TemporalMarker } from './generated/temporal_marker_pb.js';\n\nfunction buildTemporalMarker(marker) {\n  const pb = new TemporalMarker();\n  pb.setId(marker.id);\n  pb.setTrackId(marker.track_id);\n  pb.setTick(marker.tick);\n  pb.setCreatedAt(marker.created_at_ms);\n  pb.setEchoCycle(marker.echo_cycle);\n  pb.setStability(marker.stability); // enum numeric value\n  return pb;\n}\n

You can then pb.serializeBinary() for compact payloads to the Global Brain / Valkey bridge.

import sovereignpb \"your/module/internal/proto/sovereign/temporal\"\n\nfunc ToPbMarker(m TemporalMarker) *sovereignpb.TemporalMarker {\n    return &sovereignpb.TemporalMarker{\n        Id:         m.ID,\n        TrackId:    uint32(m.TrackID),\n        Tick:       m.Tick,\n        CreatedAt:  m.CreatedAt.UnixMilli(),\n        EchoCycle:  m.EchoCycle,\n        Stability:  toPbStability(m.Stability),\n    }\n}\n\nfunc toPbStability(s TemporalStability) sovereignpb.TemporalStability {\n    switch s {\n    case Stable:\n        return sovereignpb.TemporalStability_STABLE\n    case Chaotic:\n        return sovereignpb.TemporalStability_CHAOTIC\n    case Metastable:\n        return sovereignpb.TemporalStability_METASTABLE\n    default:\n        return sovereignpb.TemporalStability_STABILITY_UNSPECIFIED\n    }\n}\n

☁️ Cloudflare Durable Object Binding (JS / Workers)

Install protobufjs:

bash

Load schema:

js
import protobuf from \"protobufjs\";\n\nconst root = await protobuf.load(\"temporal_marker.proto\");\nconst TemporalMarker = root.lookupType(\"sovereign.temporal.TemporalMarker\");\n

Build + serialize:

js
function buildTemporalMarker(marker) {\n  const pb = TemporalMarker.create({\n    id: marker.id,\n    track_id: marker.track_id,\n    tick: marker.tick,\n    created_at: marker.created_at_ms,\n    echo_cycle: marker.echo_cycle,\n    stability: marker.stability,\n  });\n\n  return TemporalMarker.encode(pb).finish(); // Uint8Array\n}\n

pub struct TemporalStreamService {\n    pub gossip_rx: tokio::sync::mpsc::Receiver<PbTemporalMarker>,\n}\n\n#[tonic::async_trait]\nimpl TemporalStream for TemporalStreamService {\n    async fn get_capabilities(\n        &self,\n        req: Request<TemporalStreamCapabilitiesRequest>,\n    ) -> Result<Response<TemporalStreamCapabilitiesResponse>, Status> {\n        let node_id = req.into_inner().node_id;\n        Ok(Response::new(TemporalStreamCapabilitiesResponse {\n            node_id,\n            version: \"s27-1\".into(),\n            supports_gossip: true,\n            supports_drift_enforcement: true,\n        }))\n    }\n\n    type SubscribeTemporalMarkersStream =\n        tokio_stream::wrappers::ReceiverStream<Result<TemporalMarker, Status>>;\n\n    async fn subscribe_temporal_markers(\n        &self,\n        _req: Request<TemporalStreamSubscribeRequest>,\n    ) -> Result<Response<Self::SubscribeTemporalMarkersStream>, Status> {\n        let rx = self.gossip_rx.clone();\n        let stream = tokio_stream::wrappers::ReceiverStream::new(rx)\n            .map(|m| Ok(m));\n        Ok(Response::new(stream))\n    }\n\n    type GossipTemporalMarkersStream =\n        tokio_stream::wrappers::ReceiverStream<Result<TemporalMarker, Status>>;\n\n    async fn gossip_temporal_markers(\n        &self,\n        req: Request<tonic::Streaming<TemporalMarker>>,\n    ) -> Result<Response<Self::GossipTemporalMarkersStream>, Status> {\n        let mut inbound = req.into_inner();\n        let (tx, rx) = tokio::sync::mpsc::channel(128);\n\n        tokio::spawn(async move {\n            while let Ok(Some(marker)) = inbound.message().await {\n                // ingest into Time Machine / drift stats here\n                let _ = tx.send(Ok(marker)).await;\n            }\n        });\n\n        Ok(Response::new(tokio_stream::wrappers::ReceiverStream::new(rx)))\n    }\n}\n

Invalid epochs freeze all state‑changing operations.

3.3 Autonomous Agent Swarm (NPCs)

Tier 1:

  • Trust Graph Stabilization:

    • Slow trust decay rates.

    • Reduce sensitivity to single negative events.

  • Memory Sync Smoothing:

    • Increase semantic similarity threshold for accepting new events.

Tier 2:

  • Cognitive Load Shedding:

    • Offload complex planning to fewer, more stable agents.

    • Freeze low‑priority goals; focus on survival, stability, and diplomacy.

  • Aggression Dampening:

    • Reduce likelihood of initiating combat in high‑drift zones.

Tier 3:

  • Protective Herding:

    • NPCs cluster around stable regions and avoid chaotic areas.

    • Alliances temporarily prioritize mutual defense over expansion.

4. Global Auto‑Healing Loop

Every STC epoch (7 seconds, aligned with Cloudflare alarms):

  1. Measure:

    • Compute Φ(t), node scores, drift envelope.

  2. Classify:

    • Determine drift tier (1, 2, or 3).

  3. Apply:

    • Trigger subsystem‑specific auto‑healing actions.

  4. Decay:

    • If Φ(t) decreases and stays below thresholds for N epochs, gradually:

      • restore PCI horizon

      • relax traversal throttles

      • normalize NPC trust and tactics

This creates a feedback loop: instability → backpressure → stabilization → release.

5. Implementation Hooks

  • Rust (Substrate + HyperGossip):

    • STC pallet exposes current_tier() and healing_actions() flags.

    • HyperGossip sidecar reads these and adjusts traversal, NPU usage, and marker emission.

  • Go (Valkey + Time Machine):

    • STC module adjusts CAT regen, PCI horizon, and NPC trust decay.

    • Writer/Time Machine uses STC verdict to gate rollbacks and commits.

  • Cloudflare DO:

    • Alarm loop computes Φ(t) and broadcasts drift tier to all connected nodes.

    • Edge applies movement and PCI clamps based on tier.

  • SpaceBook UI:

    • HUD shows Auto‑Healing State (e.g., “Stabilizing Drift”, “Critical Drift — Safe Mode”).

    • Visual cues for safe corridors, PCI limitations, and NPC behavioral shifts.

You now have a full auto‑healing system: the mesh detects temporal instability, applies controlled backpressure, and gradually restores normal operation once drift subsides.

If you want to go even deeper, next step would be:

Designing Player‑Visible “Temporal Engineering” Tools

Letting players actively participate in auto‑healing (deploy dampeners, stabilize NPUs, negotiate with NPCs to reduce chaos).
